newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes higher after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes higher after volatile day.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher after a day of volatile price swings in line with strong natural gas and physical power prices, market sources said Wednesday.
"How many days now has this thing been roaring? I'm not going to get in the way of it," said one trader.
Nevertheless, the "world came out to sell June COB (California-Oregon border) at $17.00," per megawatt hour (MWh), and prices may be getting toppy, he added.
Prices rose on news of an unplanned 750 MW unit outage at the Four Corners power plant in Arizona as well as a delay in restarting a 350 MW unit at the San Juan plant in New Mexico.
"We heard of a couple of units down and saw natgas rally. Prices just whipsawed today," said another market source.
He noted that hydroelectric generating capacity in the Northwest continues to run at capacity, with excess spring runoff being spilled over the dams.
As a result, "everybody is looking at gas prices and what peaking units are costing," he explained.
The June Palo Verde (PV) contract closed 46 cents higher at $22.96 after hitting a new contract high of $23.50 (corrects from $23.00).
July PV settled up 35 cents at $26.10 after hitting a new contract high of $26.50 (corrects from $26.25) and reaching as low as $25.95 per MWh.

June California Oregon Border (COB) closed up 24 cents at $16.57 per MWh after hitting a new contract high of $17.40 (corrects from $16.65) and reaching as low as $16.30, while July lost 16 cents to settle at $17.73.
NYMEX June natural gas futures closed 4.4 cents higher at $2.353 per million British thermal units.
